title: Latency-aware meritocratic splitter for prefill/decode scheduler
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode allocator uses symmetric phase-splitting heuristics that under-serve latency-sensitive interactive requests during microbursts. We have kernel cost heterogeneity (e.g., attention-dense versus sparse kernels, different quantized code paths) which makes equal phase-slices suboptimal: some prefill/decode phases have much higher per-token GPU-cost and longer kernel latency, leading to uneven tail latency and throughput drops when mixed workloads arrive.

Proposal: Implement a 'meritocratic splitter' for phase splitting and slot allocation that combines: (1) real-time kernel-cost estimates from the kernel-probe router (latency and GPU-op cost), (2) attention-density signal from the prefill KV/attn analyzer (estimates sparsity and expected KV-cache growth), and (3) a per-client latency-sensitivity credit score derived from request metadata (SLO tags, interactive flag, token-budget). The splitter weights phase-slice sizes and assignment priorities based on a merit score: latency-sensitive requests receive small fast-path slices and hedged kernel assignments, while throughput-oriented requests accrue credits and receive larger, cheaper slices.

Key design decisions: asymmetric splitting (not equal micro-slices), merit score decay window (default 5s), hedged kernel routing for high-merit urgent slices, and backpressure thresholding to prevent starvation (max credit drain per minute). The policy must integrate with existing kernel-hint orchestration and prefix/KV caching so slices maintain cache locality when beneficial.

Why different from prior schedulers: Prior work focused on proportional fairness by token share or static phase buckets. This approach explicitly mixes kernel-selection cost signals and attention sparsity into the split decision, and introduces a short-lived credit system to balance long-term fairness with short-term latency isolation.

Deliverables: design doc with offline simulation results, prototype scheduler with feature flags, e2e perf regression run, A/B rollout plan, dashboards and SLO alerts, and PR for runtime-1.21.

Risks and mitigations: risk of starvation for throughput workloads mitigated by credit decay + max-drain cap; risk of noisy kernel-cost estimates mitigated by EWMA smoothing and conservative fallback to current allocator; complexity risk mitigated by feature-flagged rollout and telemetry gated experiments.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype merges behind feature flag: ENB_MERIT_SPLITTER=true and no default user impact
p95 latency for interactive workload improves by >= 12% vs baseline under mixed load in canary cluster
Throughput (tokens/s) for sustained batch workload does not degrade by >4% in the same experiment
No request-level starvation observed in 24h soak: 99.99% of requests receive progress within configured deadline
Dashboards added: merit_score distribution, slice_size vs kernel_latency, per-client credit balance; runbook updated
Automated A/B experiment defined with traffic split and rollback conditions in console
